diagnosis: Generalized chronic periodontitis with localized advanced periodontal destruction in the mandibular anterior region, causing hopeless periodontal prognosis of teeth 33, 32, 31, 41, 42, and 43.
treatmentProvided: Initial periodontal therapy included oral hygiene instructions, full-mouth scaling and root planing, and periodontal evaluation. Under local anesthesia, crevicular incision and flap reflection were performed, followed by atraumatic extraction of hopeless teeth 33, 32, 31, 41, 42, and 43. Extraction sockets were thoroughly debrided, curetted, and irrigated. Osteotomy preparation was completed in bilateral canine regions, two endosseous titanium implants were placed in regions 33 and 43 with primary stability greater than 35 Ncm, bone grafting was placed where required, and flaps were sutured with 3-0 silk.
treatmentPlan: Preserve available bone, eliminate infection and mobile teeth, and restore esthetics and function with a fixed implant-supported mandibular anterior prosthesis. After 3 to 4 months of osseointegration, expose implants, place healing abutments, make open-tray implant impressions, fabricate an implant-supported fixed six-unit bridge from canine to canine, and deliver the final prosthesis with pontics replacing central and lateral incisors. Continue periodontal and implant maintenance every 6 months.
dietAdvice: Soft diet for 1 week after surgery.
Avoid excessive pressure on the mandibular anterior surgical site.
Use chlorhexidine mouthwash 0.2% twice daily as advised.
Attend follow-up after 7 days for suture removal.
notes: Extraoral examination: facial symmetry maintained, no swelling or tenderness, TMJ movements within normal limits.
Intraoral examination: generalized chronic periodontitis with localized severe involvement in mandibular anterior region.
Teeth 33, 32, 31, 41, 42, and 43 showed Grade II to Grade III mobility, gingival recession, deep periodontal pockets, pathological migration, and significant attachment loss.

Periodontal findings: probing depth 7-10 mm in lower anterior region, clinical attachment loss greater than 50%, severe horizontal and vertical bone loss, poor crown-root ratio, and unfavorable long-term prognosis.

Pre-operative radiograph: severe horizontal and vertical alveolar bone loss from canine to canine, bone support reduced to apical one-third of roots, widening of periodontal ligament space, loss of lamina dura, and advanced periodontal destruction.
Mandibular anterior teeth were not suitable for predictable root canal treatment, splinting, regenerative therapy, or long-term natural tooth retention.
Implant plan: two implants in regions 33 and 43, diameter 3.75-4.2 mm, length 10-13 mm, platform-level design with good primary stability.
Final prosthesis: implant-supported fixed six-unit bridge extending from canine to canine.
Postoperative care: antibiotics for 5 days, analgesics as required, chlorhexidine mouthwash 0.2% twice daily, soft diet, and 7-day suture removal.
Final outcome: improved esthetics, speech, comfort, chewing efficiency, and stable long-term fixed rehabilitation.
